anomalies.observed: Screw terminal J3 has pin 2 on the HEATER/GPIO1 net (via the wire at (54.61,88.9) to the D10 LED anode junction and label NET0004) and pin 1 wired to GND (wire from (54.61,91.44) down to (54.61,104.14) and the GND symbol #PWR024). The MCU heater-control GPIO is therefore hard-wired to ground through an external connector, bypassing the TPS1H200 switch and the R12 limiting resistor.
anomalies.expected: The heater-control GPIO should reach only the TPS1H200 IN/DIAG_EN inputs and the status LED, and the only heater connector should be J2 (OUT on pin 2, GND on pin 1) fed from the high-side switch. The spec describes a single heater output driven through the smart high-side switch, with no direct GPIO-to-ground path.

evidence.quote: Drives a single **heater output** net through a smart high-side switch (`U6`, TPS1H200AQDGNRQ1) switched from the ESP32's GPIO1, using simple bang-bang control

anomalies.impact: If anything is plugged into or jumpered across J3, GPIO1 is shorted to ground, which can damage the MCU pin and defeats the heater-driver path. The ground pin of J3 also sits on the same net as the heater return.
